title: Songwriting with Jimmy Dupree and Joe Verges
summary: He wrote tunes with Jimmy Dupree and Joe Verges; he tells of selling songs to Feist and doubts about who wrote what, Dupree's eccentricity and ASCAP.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What was the name of this violin player that used to play out at Tranchinas years ago? Piron. Piron. I'll never forget, Piron recorded a number that an old friend of mine wrote. I used to write some tunes with him. Joe Burgess and- Oh, yeah. I know Joe Burgess. Jimmy Dupree. Jimmy Dupree and I used to write songs together.
Joe was still playing. I run into him once in a while.
I love Don't Leave Me Daddy.

Well, that was one of them. Jimmy Dupree wrote Jelly Bean, too, you remember? And he used to work for Feist. Joe goes up to New York and Jimmy and I were sitting around the Elks Club in New Orleans there and we wrote a number. My cozy little blue room. In a cozy little blue room. And it was similar on a show type number. And Joe writes down, he says, I sold my half to Phil Kornheiser and Feist. What you all gonna do with your half? Two more of us, our half. He sold his half. Jimmy said, the nerve of him. How big does he think he is? He's just a half pint as it is. But Jimmy Dupree wrote a number that he sold to P. Ronheiser. It's called My Purple Rose of Cairo.
You gotta be a dope fiend to think of a title like that. And Jimmy wrote all that? Sure Jimmy wrote that number. And he just sold it to P. Ronheiser.
I don't think P. Ronheiser ever wrote any music.
Oh, I guess he had the ability to. He was pretty good.
I don't know. Pete Bocard told me he wrote all the music and P. Ronheiser wrote the work.
And Louie's supposed to have written...

I don't like to discredit anyone. No, I don't either. I didn't say that about Dupree either. But Dupree had such an imaginative mind. I've never seen anybody or met anybody like him. He was up in New York one time. Well, for instance, he came through here and he used to get letters and mail and everything. I think a lot of times he'd write himself letters and read them. He was quite a character and I often wonder what happened to him.
He got to be a member of the Society of Composers and Publishers. I do know that.
ASCAP. And of course Joe, Joe got to be a member of ASCAP also.
